Leave Policy

Human Resource Department
AMNEX INFOTECHNOLOGIES PVT. LTD.The Company provides various categories of leave to support employees' health, family
responsibilities, and personal needs. The following general rules apply to all leave types,
unless otherwise specified for a particular leave:
• The leave year is the calendar year (1 January to 31 December).
• Leave must be applied for and approved through the HRMS.
• A weekly off or declared holiday falling within a

be applied for and approved through the HRMS.
• A weekly off or declared holiday falling within a leave period, or that immediately
precedes or succeeds it, is not counted as leave
1. Casual Leave:
To meet personal emergencies.
• Entitlement: 7 days per annum. credited at the beginning of the year; for new joiners,
credited proportionately from the month of joining
• These leaves cannot be encashed or carried forward to the next year.

• Apply at least one day in advance. Where advance notice is not possible, inform the
reporting manager and apply in the system at the earliest opportunity.
• May be clubbed with other applicable leave types.
• May be applied post-dated

• If unable to report due to illness, inform the reporting manager as early as possible.
• Sick leave of 3 or more consecutive days requires a medical certificate from a registered

3. Earned Leave:
Earned leave allows employees to take a planned break; applications should be made in
advance so the reporting manager can plan the work accordingly
• Entitlement: 21 days per calendar year, credited monthly from 1 st January. For new
joiners, proportionately, leaves will be credited.

will be visible in HRMS only after successful completion of the probation period . Once
they have achieved this milestone, the eligible leave balance for the entire period will be

is not eligible for EL encashment.

• EL cannot be applied post-dated, must be applied in advance or on the same day.• Application of such leaves must be applied well in advance, to enable the reporting
manager to plan for contingencies and work cover.
4. Paternity Leave:
Paternity Leave is granted to employees on becoming a parent to support and bond with the
new child.
• Eligibility

granted to employees on becoming a parent to support and bond with the
new child.
• Eligibility: All male employees, including biological, adoptive and commissioning fathers.
• Entitled to 14 days of Paternity Leave for each childbirth, or for each adoption or
commissioning arrangement (from the date the child is handed over).
• The leave must be availed within 6 months of the birth, and, in the case of adoption or
commissioning, within 6 months

of the birth, and, in the case of adoption or
commissioning, within 6 months of the date the child is handed over. This may be taken
in parts or in a single stretch.
• This leave must be applied in advance; it cannot be backdated

5. Maternity Leave:
Eligible female employees are entitled to paid maternity leave as per the Maternity Benefit
Act, 1961 (as amended in 2017) and the Company’s Maternity

Act, 1961 (as amended in 2017) and the Company’s Maternity Benefit Policy.
• Biological mothers: 26 weeks of paid leave for each maternity.
• Adoptive and commissioning mothers: 12 weeks of paid leave for each adoption or
commissioning arrangement, from the date the child is handed over to the mother.
• Up to 8 weeks of leave may be availed before the expected delivery date, with the balance
taken post-childbirth.

For eligibility criteria, additional benefits and the procedure for availing the leave, refer to
Section 11.31 – Maternity Benefit Policy of the handbook
6. Leaves for Miscarriage:
To recover from the Mental and physical impact of Miscarriage.
• Eligibility: 6 weeks for all female employees, immediately following the day of miscarriage
or medical termination of pregnancy, on production

all female employees, immediately following the day of miscarriage
or medical termination of pregnancy, on production of the prescribed proof. To be applied
following the event, with the prescribed proof.

7. Leave for Tubectomy Operation:
To recover from a tubectomy procedure
• Eligibility: 2 weeks for all female employees, immediately following the day of the
operation, on production of the prescribed proof.
• Must be applied in advance; cannot be backdated.

8. Special Leave:
Such leaves are granted to let the employee enjoy special personal occasions
• Eligibility: All Employees
• Entitlement: 1 day for the employee's own birthday; 1 day for their wedding anniversary;
3 days for the employee's own marriage.
• If the special leave falls on a weekend or a declared holiday, it cannot be transferred or
availed on any other day. This leave must

a declared holiday, it cannot be transferred or
availed on any other day. This leave must be applied in advance and cannot be
backdated.9. Bereavement Leave:
This leave is granted on the death of an immediate family member.
• Eligibility: All Employees are entitled for 3 days leave in case of death of an immediate
family member. Immediate family member includes: parents, grandparents, parents -In-
law, siblings, spouse and children.

10. Leave Without Pay:
Leave Without Pay applies when an employee needs to take leave but does not have
sufficient leave balance to cover it.
• Eligibility: all employees.
• Where CL and EL are exhausted, further leave availed is treated as Leave Without Pay
• As an exception to the general leave rules, where LWP is taken continuously for an entire
week, or on any working day immediately

rules, where LWP is taken continuously for an entire
week, or on any working day immediately preceding or succeeding a weekend, the
intervening weekends and declared holidays are also counted for loss-of-pay deduction.
• In medical cases, special approval may be considered subject to submission of a valid
medical certificate.
11. Sabbatical Leave:
A sabbatical is an extended break granted to long-tenured employees to attend to personal
needs or to take time away from work, in

long-tenured employees to attend to personal
needs or to take time away from work, in support of well-being and work–life balance.
• Eligibility: employees who have completed at least 3 years of service.
• An eligible employee may apply for a sabbatical of between 30 and 60 days.
• Sabbaticals require the approval of the BU Head/Department Head and the HR Head.
• A sabbatical is treated as Leave Without Pay for the period

and the HR Head.
• A sabbatical is treated as Leave Without Pay for the period

12. Election Leave:
To enable employees to exercise their constitutional right to vote during elections.
• Eligibility: all e mployees who are registered voters in the constituency where polling is
being conducted.
• A paid leave to vote on the day of polling for the employee's registered constituency, as
notified by the Election Commission of India or the relevant State Election Authority.
Local employees registered to

notified by the Election Commission of India or the relevant State Election Authority.
Local employees registered to vote in or near their work location are granted sufficient
paid time off to cast their vote; out -of-station employees whose registered constituency
is elsewhere are granted a paid day off, recognising the time needed for travel.
• The leave is applicable only on the official voting day corresponding to the employee’s
registered constituency.
• Employees must apply for the leave in advance through the HRMS,

employee’s
registered constituency.
• Employees must apply for the leave in advance through the HRMS, uploading their valid
Voter ID, so that HR can verify the registered constituency and the applicable polling date.
• Where operational requirements exist, employees must inform their reporting manager
in advance regarding their requirement to avail time off for voting.
• Election Leave cannot be carried forward or encashed.

13. Holidays:
The Company recognises holidays as time for rest, celebration, and cultural observance,
and

Holidays:
The Company recognises holidays as time for rest, celebration, and cultural observance,
and publishes a holiday calendar each year aligned to government notifications and the
needs of a diverse workforce.Public Holidays:
The Company publishes a list of fixed public holidays for each calendar year, prepared with
reference to the official holiday schedules issued by the Central Government and the
applicable State Government(s). The holidays are selected to reflect the cultural and social
diversity of the workforce. The fixed holiday

holidays are selected to reflect the cultural and social
diversity of the workforce. The fixed holiday list is published in the HRMS by 1 January each
year.
Optional Holidays:
• In addition to the fixed public holidays, employees are granted 2 optional holidays per
calendar year, to be chosen from a list of optional holidays published by the Company.
• Optional holidays must be applied for in advance through the HRMS.
• Optional holidays cannot be carried forward or encashed.
• The

in advance through the HRMS.
• Optional holidays cannot be carried forward or encashed.
• The optional holiday list is published in the HRMS by 1 January each year.
Project-Site Employees:
Employees deployed at a client site follow the holiday schedule of that site.
